critique.cause: 问题列仅100px，文字宽度为79px；为了让链接完整单行，链接列占用了220px。

critique.problems: 链接列留白较多，而回答更拥挤；部分回答多出一行，拉高对应行，整表的阅读节奏变长。
critique.cause: 链接列增至213px，挤占回答列至209px；减少的回答宽度使部分文字跨过换行阈值。

cells.text: 问题
回答
相关链接
电子发票与纸质发票具有同等法律效力吗？
具有。根据《中华人民共和国发票管理办法》及国家税务总局相关规定，符合规定的电子发票与纸质发票法律效力相同，可作为报销、维
https://www.chinatax.gov.cn/
开具电子发票后还能换开纸质发票吗？
通常不能重复开具。电子发票开具后，如需红冲或换开，应先按规定作废或开具红字发票，再由销售方重新开具；具体操作以当地税务系
https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn/
电子发票没有加盖发票专用章，是否有效？
符合条件的电子发票可以没有实体发票专用章。通过税务数字账户或全国增值税发票查验平台查验时，电子签名可替代实体章；但打印件
https://inv-veri.chinatax.gov.cn/
如何查验电子发票的真伪？
可登录全国增值税发票查验平台，输入发票号码、开票日期、金额等信息进行查验；部分电子发票还可通过税务数字账户直接查看状态。
https://inv-veri.chinatax.gov.cn/
电子发票重复报销如何防范？
单位应建立电子发票台账，登记发票号码、金额和报销日期，并在报销环节查重；也可借助财务系统或税务数字账户的发票归集功能进行
https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/
个人收到电子发票后需要保存多久？
用于报销的电子发票，建议按单位财务制度长期保存原始电子文件，不要只保留截图或打印件。涉及个人所得税专项附加扣除等事项的，
https://www.chinatax.gov.cn/

understanding.purpose: 帮助读者查找电子发票的常见问题，并阅读对应的解答和相关链接。
understanding.reading: 读者先扫描首列问题，找到所需主题后横向阅读回答，再按需使用同一行的链接；回答较长，预计会决定多数行的高度，问题和链接可在这些行高中适度换行。
groups: 问题与回答构成每行的问答对，应通过同一行的对齐关系保持关联。
相关链接是各问题的补充入口，与同一行的问答关联，但承担导航而非解释作用。
keep_intact: 相关链接中最长的连续字符串，至少需要175px文字宽度。
问题和回答中的连续词语及标识符应保持完整。
may_wrap: 问题可按中文自然断行，但应保持易于逐行扫描。
回答可按中文自然断行；长回答会形成较高的行。
链接文字中允许断行的部分可换行。

bad.why: The question column would fragment the bold row labels into short lines, while the link column would be narrower than the 175px unbreakable URL segment plus padding, risking overflow or broken identifiers.

contrast.why: The question column would fragment the bold row labels into short lines, while the link column would be narrower than the 175px unbreakable URL segment plus padding, risking overflow or broken identifiers.

final.rationale: r1B gives the questions enough width to remain easy to scan while leaving a substantial measure for the longer answers. Its link column accommodates the longest unbreakable URL segment, although two links wrap at a hyphen. r2C gains shorter answer blocks, but its narrower questions break into more lines and weaken the scan down the first column.

general: Give row labels enough width to support scanning, even when another column contains more text.
Protect long identifiers from forced breaks, and judge the remaining width by how the columns work together.
specific: The answers carry most of the prose, but the questions are the entry points to this FAQ.
At 196px, the link column fits the longest unbreakable segment but wraps the two inv-veri URLs.

final.tradeoffs: r2C and r3C devote more room to answers and reduce table height, at the cost of more fragmented questions. r1C keeps the URLs on one line but narrows the answers and makes several rows taller.
final.uncertain: A designer who prioritizes uninterrupted links or shorter answers over scanning the questions could reasonably prefer r1C or r2C. The ranges are conservative estimates based on the rendered candidates; intermediate widths have not been individually verified.

A.why: The answer column has useful width, but the questions break into many short fragments and every link wraps, making both row identification and URLs harder to scan.

B.why: Questions remain reasonably scannable and all URLs stay on one line. The answer column is rather narrow, creating tall rows and substantial empty space under the links.

C.why: The questions retain a readable measure and the answers have more room than in B. Two URLs wrap at the hyphen, while most remain intact.

D.why: The wide question column is easy to scan, but the answers are squeezed into short lines and the links wrap, producing tall rows with much unused space.

E.why: Questions are reasonably readable, but the narrow answer column produces tall rows, and two URLs wrap despite the generous link column.

F.why: The answers have a comfortable width, but the narrow question column breaks row labels into many short lines. Two URLs wrap at the hyphen.

reviews.unsure: B keeps every URL intact, while C gives the longer answers more room at the cost of wrapping two URLs. Their relative merit depends on whether readers primarily scan links or read answers.

A.why: The questions are easy to scan, but the answer column is cramped into many short lines, making the rows very tall. Several URLs also wrap.

B.why: The answer column reads comfortably, but the very narrow question column breaks row labels into four or five short lines. Several URLs also split awkwardly.

C.why: Questions remain reasonably scannable and all URLs stay on one line. The answer column is somewhat narrow, producing long rows and substantial empty space under the links.

D.why: Questions are reasonably scannable and answers have a little more room than in C. The two verification URLs wrap after the hyphen, while the link column still occupies considerable space.

E.why: The answers have a useful width, but questions wrap into several short lines, weakening the row labels. Two verification URLs also wrap.

F.why: The question and answer columns have a useful balance, with readable row labels and fewer short answer lines than C or D. Two verification URLs wrap after the hyphen.

reviews.unsure: C keeps every URL on one line, so it may be preferable if preserving complete link text is more important than giving the answers additional width.
